subject: Clarify private resolution authority, cert bindings, and proxy behavior for acme-corp deployment
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acme-corp.com>

Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — cert & resolver questions before kick-off

Hi Laura / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Before our infra team signs off on the on-prem package we need a couple of clarifications around how Redwood will handle private name resolution and TLS for our private endpoints in our VPC:

1) Which party is the authoritative owner of the private FQDNs (e.g. api.private.acme.internal) once the private deployment is installed? Do we continue to own the zone and provide nameservers, or should we handover a subset of records to Redwood?

2) For TLS termination: will Redwood terminate mTLS at our edge (customer-managed ingress), or do you expect Redwood to terminate inside the VPC on the serving hosts and present SANs that match our internal names?

3) If Redwood terminates TLS inside the VPC, how are cert rotations handled operationally? We need an audit-friendly process and clear ownership for CSR generation and key custody.

I attached a quick diagram the team sketched during the call. Can your infra folks annotate the ideal responsibilities so we can update our procurement and security docs?

We'd like to get this cleared this week to avoid slipping the install window.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of Platform Security
Acme Corp

Ellen — thanks for the clear list. I looped in Ben and Karthik from infra (cc'd) to provide the technical plan. Quick answers up-front so procurement can proceed:

- Ownership model: customer-owned zone with delegated sub-zone for Redwood-managed records is our preferred pattern, but we can support DNS-over-proxy (no delegation) if your security team prefers full custody.
- TLS termination: default model is Redwood terminates inside the VPC on host-level terminating proxies. We can also support reverse-proxy termination at your edge if you insist on customer-side termination.
- Cert rotations: we recommend automated CSR rotation with customer approval flow for key custody — see proposed matrix from Ben below.

Ben / Karthik: could you provide the annotated diagram and a short step-by-step cert rotation playbook (including required Drive links) — Ellen asked for auditability and an owner map.

Action items: 1) Ben: matrix + checklist 2) Karthik: annotated diagram showing resolver flow 3) Laura/Marissa: confirm procurement checklist and gating items.

I copied procurement so they're aware of these options. Ellen — we'll try to get a consolidated doc by EOD.

Best,

Ellen — attaching the cert-binding matrix and a short playbook. High level notes here so it's searchable in the thread:

- Preferred DNS approach (recommended): Acme owns acme.internal. You delegate a single sub-zone under acme.internal (e.g. redwood.acme.internal) to our nameservers via NS records. Delegation limits blast radius and allows us to programmatically manage records for cluster endpoints, SRV/TTL tuning, and automated failover.

- Alternative (customer-managed only): If delegation is disallowed, we provide a lightweight DNS proxy sidecar that forwards resolution to your resolvers; we do not store zone data in that mode. That increases latency for some internal checks and complicates autoscaling fallback, but is supported.

- TLS termination modes:
  * Redwood-terminates-internal (default): We run an internal terminating proxy (iptables/route to proxy) on the serving subnet. The proxy presents certs with SANs for the redwood-managed FQDNs. Client mutual-auth is supported if you enable mTLS at the client side.
  * Customer-terminates-edge (optional): You terminate TLS at your edge LB and forward proxied plain HTTP to Redwood inside the VPC over the private network. In this case Redwood expects an authenticated tunnel (mTLS between edge and Redwood) and does not present internal SANs.

- Cert rotation: we recommend an automated CSR cycle where Redwood generates a CSR on the host, sends it to your CA via a signed request, and the issued cert is pushed back to the host. For customers that require key custody, we support HSM-backed creation controlled by the customer (we provide the orchestration hooks and an operator-runner). Rotation cadence is configurable (default 90 days).

See attached cert-binding-matrix.xlsx and redwood-private-tls-checklist.pdf.

Ellen — I took your sketch and annotated a recommended resolution flow. Key excerpt pasted below; full PNG attached.

--- annotated excerpt ---
1) Upstream ownership: Acme retains acme.internal as the authoritative zone. We request NS delegation for redwood.acme.internal to our managed nameservers. Delegation record example: redwood.acme.internal. IN NS ns1.redwood.local.

2) Resolver placement: Two resolver modes supported:
   - Split-resolver (recommended): Redwood runs an internal resolver that only resolves redwood.* records locally and forwards all other queries to your instance metadata resolvers. This keeps your internal names authoritative while allowing Redwood to manage service records.
   - Proxy-resolver (no delegation): Sidecar that proxies queries to your resolvers and caches negative results locally for short TTLs.

3) Cert binding: For delegated mode we issue certs with CN/SAN set to redwood-managed FQDNs. For proxy mode we rely on your edge certs and establish mTLS between your edge and our internal proxies.

4) Rotation process (audit-friendly):
   - Step A (CSR generation): Either Redwood-generated CSR (default) OR customer-provided CSR when key custody is required.
   - Step B (Approval): CSR is submitted to Acme's CA via a signed request to the CA API. The CA issues cert; the issuance event is logged in both Redwood and Acme audit trails.
   - Step C (Push & verify): New cert is pushed to terminating proxies and integrated tests (SNI checks, mTLS handshake) are run automatically.

--- end excerpt ---

- For audit reasons we want to keep key custody in our HSM for the first rotation cycle, then evaluate moving to Redwood-managed CSR automation after 3 months. Karthik: can you confirm the HSM-backed CSR flow will surface CA issuance events in our audit log (we use Splunk)?
